title: Computer Science and Development Foundations
purpose: Understand how computers, operating systems, networks, and software development tools work.

topics.title: Computer Fundamentals
guidance: Practical: Understand the role of CPU, RAM, storage, and GPU in a computer that runs AI applications.

topics.title: Operating Systems
guidance: Practical: Inspect running processes and resource usage on a computer.

topics.title: Computer Networking
guidance: Practical: Make API requests and inspect network traffic through browser developer tools and Postman.

topics.title: Command Line and Linux
subtopics: Create, copy, move, and delete operations
guidance: Practical: Set up a Linux environment and run a small Python project.

topics.title: Git and GitHub
guidance: Practical: Create a repository, commit code, branch, merge, and document a project.

title: Programming Languages and Python Engineering
purpose: Build strong programming fundamentals and make Python the primary language for AI engineering.

title: Mathematics, DSA, and Problem Solving
purpose: Build the mathematical and algorithmic foundation needed for ML and reliable software engineering.

topics.title: Discrete Mathematics and Logic
guidance: Why: Useful for algorithms, computer science, graph-based knowledge systems, and logical problem solving.

topics.title: Information Theory Basics
subtopics: Why these concepts appear in ML and language models

topics.title: Data Structures and Algorithms
guidance: Practical: Solve beginner-to-intermediate programming problems regularly. Include progress tracking for DSA practice.

title: Software Engineering, Databases, and Data Engineering
purpose: Learn how to design maintainable applications and prepare data for real-world AI workloads.

topics.title: NoSQL Fundamentals
subtopics: Choosing a database based on requirements
guidance: Include MongoDB as an introductory document database.

topics.title: Data Engineering Fundamentals
subtopics: Apache Spark fundamentals as an advanced optional topic

topics.title: Data Modeling and Storage for AI

title: Data Science and Machine Learning
purpose: Learn how data is analyzed and how ML algorithms identify patterns and make predictions.

topics.title: Data Science Fundamentals
subtopics: AI vs ML vs Data Science

topics.title: Model Training and Improvement
guidance: Practical projects:
- Student performance prediction.
- House price prediction.
- Spam classifier.
- Customer segmentation.

title: Deep Learning and PyTorch
purpose: Understand neural networks and the mechanics of training more complex machine learning models.

topics.title: GPU and Model Training Fundamentals
guidance: Keep low-level CUDA programming and advanced distributed training optional.

title: NLP, Transformers, and Large Language Models
purpose: Understand how LLMs process text, represent information, and generate responses.

topics.title: Prompt Engineering and Context Design
guidance: Prompting complements software architecture, evaluation and security; it cannot replace them.
General concepts transfer across providers, while API message roles and schema features must be checked in that provider’s current documentation.

topics.title: LLM Training and Adaptation
guidance: Explain training vs fine-tuning vs inference clearly.

title: Backend, AI Application Engineering, and LLM Integration
purpose: Turn AI models into real software applications.

topics.title: Token and Cost Engineering
guidance: Explain that LLM text tokens, authentication tokens, and API keys are different concepts.

title: RAG, Graph RAG, Agents, and Knowledge Systems
purpose: Build AI applications that work with external knowledge, tools, and multi-step tasks.

topics.title: Vector Databases
guidance: Do not require learning every vector database. PostgreSQL with pgvector can be the first practical option.

topics.title: Graph RAG
subtopics: Combining vector search and graph search
Feeding retrieved graph context to an LLM
guidance: Explain that Graph RAG is not a universal replacement for traditional RAG.

topics.title: AI Frameworks and Protocols
guidance: Learn core concepts before becoming dependent on any one framework.

title: System Design, Distributed Systems, and Scalability
purpose: Build systems that can handle growing users, traffic, workloads, and AI inference demand without becoming unreliable.

topics.title: Load and Stress Testing
guidance: Practical: Test your own API under controlled loads, starting with small traffic levels. Do not claim million-request capacity without evidence.

title: Security, Testing, Cloud, DevOps, and MLOps
purpose: Make the application secure, reliable, observable, maintainable, and deployable.

topics.title: Cloud Computing
guidance: Learn one cloud provider deeply at first: AWS or GCP.
Azure can be explored later if a job or project requires it.

topics.title: DevOps and CI/CD
guidance: Kubernetes and advanced Terraform are later-stage skills, not prerequisites for the first working AI application.

topics.title: Privacy, Governance, and Responsible AI
subtopics: Awareness of applicable privacy and compliance requirements
guidance: For legal and regulatory content, do not present outdated legal advice. Direct learners to current official government and regulatory sources.

title: Advanced AI Systems Architecture
purpose: Combine previous skills to design advanced, reliable AI infrastructure.

topics.title: Intelligent Model Routing
subtopics: Easy, medium, and complex task levels

topics.title: Model Serving and Inference Optimization
subtopics: Hugging Face Text Generation Inference overview
guidance: Treat advanced serving frameworks as practical exploration topics. Do not require mastery of all frameworks.
